checks.note: The rationale and limitations match e1: PC Gamer reported on 2026-10-21 that Amazon took about $5B of NVIDIA racks in August that it could not yet deploy. The 2022-01-01 to 2026-09-22 cohort and the installation reference point are both visible. The problem is the e1 excerpt. 'Early Rack' cuts off the process name 'Early Rack Receipt' partway through. As a result the excerpt does not show the source sentence and conveys nothing of what the item supports.

The rationale correctly says UBP estimated 'more than $1.25 trillion' on 2026-09-16, and the unresolved causal outcome matches the reviews. However, the e1 excerpt 'USD 1.25 trillion' drops the source's qualifier 'more than', so the cited quote reads as an exact figure rather than a lower bound. The proposition leaves out the speaker's mechanism ('massive amounts of capital', 'ridiculous demands'), but the full excerpt shows it, so this is minor.

Both excerpts are full sentences from the sources. Meta (D&A higher, net income higher, $9.89B litigation charge) and Alphabet (depreciation higher, net income lower, $6.7B equity-loss effect) are stated as in e1 and e2 for July-September 2026. Saying the quarter 'mostly precedes' the September 22 post is accurate. The limitations say plainly that only two of the four companies are covered, that D&A is combined, and that there is no deadline. The open horizon and unresolved outcome match the reviews.

The rationale matches the evidence: Microsoft added another gigawatt in April-June 2026 and is bringing capacity online faster than ever (e1), and Alphabet described supply constraints on July 22 (e2). The April-June period and the scope of 'everybody' are visible. The e1 excerpt, though, is the single word 'faster', cut from 'bringing capacity online faster than ever'. On its own it does not show the source's statement. The e2 excerpt is shortened but still faithful.
